# FR-212 — Go global: delegate skill + MCP projection to npx tools, retire per-project install

**Type:** Feature / Refactor · **Priority:** P1-High · **Effort:** L-Large (likely parent + children at PLANNING) · **Status:** Ready
**Resolves:** FR-208 (custom-vs-delegate → DELEGATE, README-grounded 2026-06-26)
**Supersedes:** TD-235, BR-071 · **Folds:** FR-184 (residual) · **Narrows:** FR-124 (→ agents compiler only) · **Retires:** the FR-191 per-project symlink layer.

## Decision (FR-208 resolved)
Delegate the two commoditized projection surfaces to external distributors instead of maintaining custom logic:
- **Skills → `npx skills`** (vercel-labs/skills — 72 agents, auto-detect, local-path sources, `remove`/prune, global/project scope, symlink mode).
- **MCP → `npx add-mcp`** (neon-solutions/add-mcp — 15 agents, auto-detect, `${VAR}` secret indirection, JSON + Codex TOML, `-g` global).

Grounded in the tools' current READMEs (2026-06-26). The #832 premise (FR-202 M1, 2026-06-22: "npx doesn't cover our harnesses") has **flipped** per the READMEs; a real smoke test confirms before any custom code is retired.

## The actual surfaces (corrected — was wrong in the FR-208 framing)
Projection surfaces are **agents · skills · mcp · hooks** (`core/scripts/cli-adapters/surfaces-manifest.json` = agents+skills; CLI validator `cli/src/verbs/harness.ts:67` = `agents|skills|mcp|hook`). There is **no rules surface** (retired FR-187) and **no prompts surface** (`core/os/` is boot-loaded, not projected).
- **Delegated:** skills, mcp.
- **Stays custom:** agents (the `harness-manifest.json` compiler) + hooks (capability-bound; TD-217 frontier).

## HARD CONSTRAINT — wrap, do NOT replace (operator)
No `igris` verb is deleted or changes signature. `igris add/remove skill`, `igris install`, `igris harness compile`, and the MCP-register path keep their UX + Igris-specific logic (canonical core ownership, registry/personal overlay, scoping, the FR-184 grant). What swaps is the *placement engine underneath*: custom `compile_harnesses.sh` (skills) + `mcp-register.ts` (config-merge) → a shell-out to the **pinned** external tools. The verb is the abstraction seam; consumers never see the tool change, and we can swap/drop the tool later without breaking a command.

## Pillar 1 — delegate the 2 commoditized surfaces
### Skills → `npx skills`
- `igris add skill` / `add --core skill`: own/vendor as today (core in `~/.igris/core/skills/`, personal in the registry) → delegate *placement* to `npx skills` (local-path source, all detected harnesses, **`-g` global**, symlink mode).
- `igris remove skill` / `--core`: delegate → `npx skills remove` (the inverse BR-071 lacked + the prune TD-235 lacked).
- Retire: the skills surface of `compile_harnesses.sh`.

### MCP → `npx add-mcp`
- Delegate `igris-brain` registration → `npx add-mcp` (auto-detect, **`-g` global**, JSON + Codex TOML).
- Secrets: use `${VAR}` indirection if any harness config would carry a secret (igris-brain reads `remote_brain.api_key` from `~/.igris/config.json` today, so verify whether any is needed — never write a literal).
- **FR-184 residual (kept custom):** `add-mcp --auto-approve` grants the no-prompt wildcard only for **Codex + Claude**. For **Antigravity / Gemini / OpenCode**, keep a thin Igris step writing the FULL wildcard grant (`mcp(igris-brain/*)` etc.) + a drift invariant.
- Retire: the config-merge in `mcp-register.ts` (keep the 3-harness grant adapter + drift check).

## Pillar 2 — surfaces global, install → register-only
**Goal:** one portable overlay, installed once globally; a project's only per-project state is its brain registration (which doubles as the hook-gate). Kills the per-project "shape" that's hard to keep uniform — the whole point is to move your setup everywhere.

Current `igris install <project>` (`cli/src/verbs/install.ts`) does, per-project: `.claude/agents`+`.claude/skills` symlinks (step 3), `.claude/settings.json` hooks merge (step 6), `.igris_version` (step 5) — plus brain register (7), installed_features (8), global MCP (11). Steps 3/5/6 duplicate what a global projection provides.

Change:
- **All surfaces project GLOBALLY:** skills/MCP via npx `-g`; **agents** via the custom compiler to `~/.claude/agents` (+ the other harnesses' global agent dirs); **hooks** to `~/.claude/settings.json` (and per-harness global hook configs where supported — Claude/OpenCode).
- **`igris install <project>` reduces to `igris_project_register`** (the brain row) + any genuinely-global bookkeeping (installed_features goes global). Retire: `applySymlinkLayer` (per-project symlinks), the per-project `settings.json` merge, per-project `.igris_version`.
- **Global hooks gate on brain-registration:** global hooks fire for every project, so they must no-op unless cwd is a registered Igris project (cwd→registry lookup). Registration becomes the per-project state AND the gate, replacing today's implicit "hooks only exist in installed projects" gate.
- Keep the `igris install` verb name — it just does less (wrap, not replace).

## Dependency strategy (decided — pinned)
The npx tools ship as **pinned npm dependencies**, invoked via their local binary — offline/CI-safe + supply-chain-pinned. No `npx`-on-demand network fetch at runtime; **no custom-engine fallback** (a parallel path negates the "less code" win — reliability comes from pinning + the smoke-test, not a fallback).

## Smoke-test gate (the #832 insurance — blocks retiring ANY custom code)
On a FRESH non-igris-ai project (clean HOME/sandbox): global install → project the `boot` skill + register `igris-brain` to **all 5** harnesses via the delegated path → assert (a) skill present + usable per harness, (b) MCP responds with **no per-tool prompt** per harness (incl. the 3 needing the custom grant), (c) `igris remove skill` leaves **zero dangling**, (d) global hooks **fire in a registered project and no-op in an unregistered one**. Only after green do we retire `compile_harnesses.sh` skills + `mcp-register.ts` + `applySymlinkLayer`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every `igris` verb signature + UX unchanged (wrap, not replace) — existing verb tests still green.
- [ ] Skills add/remove/install delegate to `npx skills` (`-g`, local source, all detected, symlink); `remove` does prune + unprojection.
- [ ] MCP registration delegates to `npx add-mcp` (`-g`); no literal secret in any harness config.
- [ ] FR-184 residual: Antigravity/Gemini/OpenCode get the FULL wildcard grant + drift invariant; fresh-project no-prompt verification per harness.
- [ ] All surfaces (skills/agents/mcp/hooks) install GLOBALLY; `igris install <project>` reduces to brain registration.
- [ ] Global hooks gate on brain-registration: fire in a registered project, no-op in an unregistered one (test both).
- [ ] npx tools pinned as deps (no runtime fetch); offline install works.
- [ ] Smoke-test gate green on all 5 before any custom code is retired.
- [ ] Retired: `compile_harnesses.sh` skills surface · `mcp-register.ts` merge · `applySymlinkLayer` per-project layer. Untouched: the agents compiler.
- [ ] Docs (multi-cli.md, SETUP_GUIDE, UPDATE_GUIDE, `--help`) + §13 enumeration surfaces updated; TD-096 mirror for any `core/` change.

## Risks
- Supply-chain / version drift on 2 external deps → pin + CI smoke-test.
- README over-claim (the #832 ghost) → the smoke-test gate is the hard guard; don't retire custom code until green.
- `npx skills` placement semantics differ per harness (opencode wrapper vs symlink) → verify in the smoke test.
- add-mcp `--auto-approve` format (wildcard vs enumerated) for Codex/Claude → verify wildcard, else treat like the other 3.
- Global hooks firing in non-Igris projects if the gate misfires → the registered-vs-unregistered gate test is mandatory.

## Out of scope
- Agents projection (stays on the custom compiler); rules/prompts (not surfaces); hooks (capability-bound, TD-217).
- Layer-2 customization registry (FR-139).
- Re-deciding canonical-as-SSOT.
